findings.problem: `spatialWeight` and `spatialPoint` re-implement the fiber-sum pushforward of a simplex point along a map of vertex sets. Their weight at `i` is the sum of `w j` over all `j` with `f j = i`, where `f = Fin.cast _ ∘ staircaseSpatial p k`. The project already has this as `FiniteSimplex.map f`, which also proves nonnegativity, total mass, composition, vertex behaviour and continuity (`continuous_map`). Mathlib has the same operation as `StdSimplex.map` with `continuous_map`. Here the nonneg and sum-to-one proofs are redone with `Finset.sum_comm`. `chart` then spends about 15 lines re-proving continuity of the same sum with `continuous_pi`, `continuous_finsetSum` and `split_ifs`. `intervalWeight` and `intervalPoint` repeat the pattern for the map `staircaseTime k : Fin (p+1) → Fin 2` (weight of the vertex `1`). The result is a second, private pushforward API for `Delta`-type simplices.
findings.proposed_change: Define the staircase vertex map `f : Fin (p+1) → Fin (p-1+1)` as `Fin.cast … ∘ staircaseSpatial p k`. Define `spatialPoint` as `StandardSimplex.ofDelta (FiniteSimplex.map f (StandardSimplex.toDelta w))`, or work in `Delta` throughout. Keep the name `spatialPoint` and add a lemma `spatialPoint_apply` for the fiber-sum formula, so SubdivisionPrismAffine.lean can use it instead of unfolding `spatialWeight`. Take `chart`'s spatial continuity from `FiniteSimplex.continuous_map f` composed with `affineCompMap`'s continuity. Likewise express `intervalWeight k w` as `FiniteSimplex.map (staircaseTime k) … 1`.
findings.benefit: This removes the duplicated nonneg, sum and continuity proofs and the roughly 15-line manual continuity argument. It also lets the existing `map_comp_apply` and `map_vertex` lemmas apply to the prism chart. The staircase chart becomes a visible pushforward, so a reader sees it is the standard simplex map and does not have to re-check the fiber-sum bookkeeping.
